explanation: This theorem is about definitions that belong to the library itself: `coord`, `coordEquiv`, `stdBasisVec` and `stdFullLattice`, all defined in the same file. The proof rewrites with two lemmas that are also in that file, `coord_tmul` and `coordEquiv_stdBasisVec`, then splits on whether i = j. The mathematical content is that this concrete coordinate map sends the basis vector `b ⊗ e_j` to `if i = j then b else 0`. In Mathlib terms that combines `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis_repr_tmul` with `Basis.repr_self`/`Finsupp.single_apply`. Getting there means unfolding several library definitions and chaining more than one Mathlib result, so no single Mathlib declaration states or directly specialises to this. I read the relevant definitions in the file and looked for a Mathlib lemma that matches directly; I found none.
